PullRequest.Title: ci: run Agent Host E2E tests in their own job
PullRequest.Body:
> [!NOTE]
> Stacked on #342729: it reuses that PR's `required-checks` job. This PR targets `main` so that its CI runs, so please review only the last commit, `ci: run Agent Host E2E tests in their own job`.

Agent Host E2E is the slowest part of the `<OS> / Electron` job, and on Windows that job is the slowest check in a pull request run. On runs where Agent Host E2E runs, `Windows / Electron` takes about 37.5 minutes: 10.9 of setup, 15.0 of Agent Host E2E and 11.7 of integration tests (7 of the last 12 successful runs). #342346 moved the suites into their own script and step, and #342492 runs them as their own Azure DevOps job. This PR does the same for GitHub Actions, as #342346 suggested.

## Changes

- **Detection moves to `Detect Changes`.**
  - The `changes` job runs `detect-agent-host-e2e-changes` once and exposes `agent-host-e2e`, `agent-host-test-profile` and `agent-host-test-profile-reason`.
  - The in-job detection step and `VSCODE_SKIP_AGENT_HOST_E2E` are removed from the three test workflows.
- **A new `<OS> (run) / Agent-Host-E2E` job per platform.**
  - It runs the `🧪 Run Agent Host E2E tests (Electron)` step on its own machine, in parallel with `<OS> (run) / Electron`.
  - It is skipped when the changes cannot affect the suites, and runs when detection fails.
  - It doesn't compile the integration test extensions, which the suites don't use.
- **The required `<OS> / Electron` check is unchanged.** `required-checks` (from #342729) now reports it from both the integration tests job and the Agent Host E2E job. A skipped Agent Host E2E job only passes when detection succeeded and reported `agent-host-e2e: false`.
- **The profile still reaches both jobs.** Both jobs receive the Agent Host test profile as workflow inputs, which fall back to `full`. The provider integration tests in the Electron integration job still read it.
- **Unique names:**
  - The job artifacts get an `-agent-host-e2e` suffix.
  - The Windows `JobId` runner label is unique because it includes the job name.
  - On Windows, the integration diagnostics steps also run in the Agent Host E2E job.
- **Docs and tests:** the E2E README and the `integration-tests` skill describe the new job, and `agentHostTestSelection.test.ts` now checks the new wiring.

## Expected impact

When Agent Host E2E runs (about half of PRs), `<OS> / Electron` should finish sooner:

| Platform | Before | After (estimate) |
|---|---|---|
| Windows | ~37.5 min | ~26 min |
| Linux | ~18 min | ~12 min |
| macOS | ~13.5 min | ~9 min |

The trade-off is a second machine setup per platform: about 11 runner-minutes on the Windows 1ES pool, and 2–3 minutes each on Linux and macOS. When the 1ES pool is saturated, the extra job also waits for a machine. The capacity #342729 frees for extension-, docs- and CLI-only PRs (about 4.4 Windows runner-minutes per run on average) partly offsets this.

## How to test

- **This PR** changes the PR workflows, so the Agent Host E2E jobs run with the `full` profile on all three platforms, in parallel with the Electron integration tests. `<OS> / Electron` should pass only once both have passed.
- **Already run:**
  - `node --test lib/test/agentHostTestSelection.test.ts lib/test/detectChanges.test.ts` in `build/`: 17 tests pass, including the rewritten wiring test and the integration/Agent Host E2E step pairing across the GitHub and Azure DevOps pipelines.
  - `actionlint` on the four workflows: only the existing unknown self-hosted runner label findings.
  - `npm run eslint` and a strict `tsc --noEmit` on the changed tests passed.
- **After merge:** a PR that changes only workbench code should show `<OS> (run) / Agent-Host-E2E` as skipped and `<OS> / Electron` as passing.

> Authored with Copilot

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The matrix cardinality, `runs-on`, `if: always()`, and one-element `parts` arrays are explicit in the changed workflow. The base diff shows Electron-Unit and Remote reusable jobs previously reported the required names directly, while only Browser and Smoke needed aggregators. The only uncertainty is exact runner queue/setup duration, not whether six runner allocations occur on every PR.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Six GitHub-hosted Ubuntu runner VMs plus their startup and jq process work per pull-request run.
Findings.PerformanceScaling: The cost is a fixed six runner allocations per workflow run and therefore grows linearly with PR update frequency and concurrent PR volume; within one run they join the 15-child reporter burst after the shared dependency barrier.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Excessive runner allocation and a burst of avoidable CI work on the required-check completion path, which can lower concurrent workflow throughput and delay status completion.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this diff, each platform's Electron-Unit and Remote reusable workflow job directly emitted its required `<OS> / <job>` status, so these six statuses required no separate reporter runners. Only the three Browser and three sharded Smoke statuses used aggregation jobs.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Every PR now expands six additional `required-checks` matrix children for the three Electron-Unit and three Remote statuses. Each child allocates an `ubuntu-24.04` runner, waits for the shared dependency barrier, runs jq over `needs`, and exits, even though its status is a direct pass-through from one test job.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added `required-checks` matrix entry at `.github/workflows/pr.yml:482` creates a reporter job for `Linux / Electron-Unit`; the same added matrix block does this for Electron-Unit and Remote on all three platforms. These six checks each have exactly one `parts` producer, unlike Electron, Browser, and sharded Smoke checks that actually require aggregation.
Findings.Title: Keep single-producer checks off the reporter matrix
Findings.Impact: Every PR consumes six unnecessary GitHub-hosted runner starts and slots after the test phase, adding final check-reporting latency when runners queue and reducing CI throughput across concurrent PRs. The waste is especially visible for documentation/Rust-only changes, where expensive tests are correctly skipped but these six VMs still start solely to relay `skipped` as success.
Findings.Evidence: `required-checks` runs on `ubuntu-24.04` with one matrix child per `check`. Six newly added entries—Electron-Unit and Remote for Linux, macOS, and Windows—contain one producer each, so they perform no aggregation. Because the job uses `if: ${{ always() }}`, these six runner VMs are requested even when change detection skipped their test jobs. The repository's changed workflow comment also establishes that a reusable workflow can preserve a required status while skipping its inner job, so these pass-through runners are not necessary to retain path-based skipping.
Findings.Recommendation: Keep aggregation only for multi-producer Electron, Browser, and Smoke checks. For Electron-Unit and Remote, pass the detection result into the reusable workflow, apply the skip condition to its inner job (the pattern documented at the top of this workflow), restore the required check name on that job, and remove these six single-part matrix entries and dependencies.

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: Agent Host E2E launched up to five test processes but the entire suite was sequenced before the Electron integration subprocess in one runner job, so integration could not start until the E2E suite completed.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: PR Windows / Electron checks that selected Agent Host E2E spent roughly 15 additional minutes on the serial critical path (about 37.5 minutes total per the traced workflow scenario), with analogous smaller delays on Linux and macOS.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: The Agent Host E2E subprocess suite now runs on a separate Windows runner in parallel with Electron integration tests, removing its approximately 15-minute suite duration from the serial Windows Electron critical path; the required check still joins both results.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: In the base workflow, blame line 233 identifies the Agent Host E2E step introduced by e886b81b9b9d4a39d8e397c33e76ce04d5cbbe85. The base diff shows that this 30-minute subprocess suite ran in the same Windows reusable-workflow job immediately before `test-integration.bat`, whose condition explicitly allowed it to proceed after the E2E step. The PR adds `windows-agent-host-e2e-tests` as a distinct reusable-workflow invocation and passes `integration_tests: false`, while the existing Electron job no longer enables Agent Host E2E, so the two runner jobs can execute concurrently.

Scenarios.Scenario: Agent Host-affecting source PR runs Electron integration and Agent Host E2E on Linux, macOS, and Windows
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The `changes` job must finish two changed-file classifications before either reusable test workflow starts. Per OS, the existing Electron integration job and the new Agent Host E2E job then run in parallel; `<OS> / Electron` waits for both through `required-checks`. The split removes the E2E suite from the integration job's serial critical path, after which the required-check reporter runner must still start and finish.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: List pull-request files through GitHub's REST API for the general and Agent Host classifiers.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two sequential `paginate(listFiles)` operations, each fetching ceil(changed-files/100) pages.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The general classifier made one call centrally; Agent Host classification made one call later inside each of the three already-allocated Electron jobs. The diff reduces total calls from four to two but moves the Agent Host call onto the common startup path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All changed core test jobs now need `changes`, so both calls complete before test runners can be allocated.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Perform an additional full LFS checkout, restore node_modules and built-in-extension caches, conditionally install/download misses, transpile sources, and set up Electron for each new Agent Host job.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One additional setup sequence per affected OS, three total; cold misses can add one dependency install and built-in/Electron downloads per OS.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Agent Host E2E reused the Electron integration job's checkout, caches, transpilation, and Electron setup, then ran serially before integration.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: This setup precedes each E2E suite, but runs in parallel with the existing integration runner rather than delaying it.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Launch the Agent Host suite runner, which starts isolated E2E test processes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One runner per OS and up to five child suites concurrently per runner.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same suite and process count ran before integration in the same OS job.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Each OS Electron required check joins this suite with integration; parallel placement removes the suite duration from the prior serial chain.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Allocate Ubuntu runners to translate test-job results into required statuses.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: 15 reporter runners per PR; six entries have only one producer and do no aggregation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Six Browser/Smoke reporters existed; Electron-Unit and Remote statuses came directly from six test jobs, and Agent Host was part of the direct Electron job.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required statuses complete only after the shared test dependency barrier and reporter startup; queueing can extend the final gate.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One workflow run per PR update; setup scales across three operating systems, the REST work scales by changed-file pages, E2E subprocesses are capped at five per OS, and reporter demand is a fixed 15-job burst per run.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Three OS-level Agent Host jobs can run alongside three integration jobs. Each Agent Host runner launches one process per entrypoint with a shared limit of five processes per OS. Windows uses a finite self-hosted 1ES pool; Linux/macOS use separate hosted runners. The required-check phase can request all 15 matrix reporters together.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Each new OS job independently restores node_modules and built-in-extension caches. Warm hits avoid dependency installs/downloads but still pay checkout, cache restore, transpilation, and Electron setup; cold misses duplicate downloads/install work relative to the previously shared integration runner. No cross-job coalescing is present.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: workflow conditions, job dependencies, cache steps, and subprocess limits were traced directly. The serial-path fix was also tied by base blame to its introducing commit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact runner queue and warm/cold setup times vary, but the three additional setup sequences, bounded E2E concurrency, serial-before/parallel-after call path, and six unnecessary single-producer reporter allocations are explicit.
Scenarios.Verdict: The heavy-job split is an intentional bounded resource-for-latency tradeoff and fixes a concrete serial regression, so it is not a finding. The six single-producer required-check reporters add avoidable runner work without enabling aggregation and were reported as a medium concurrency-burst issue.

Scenarios.Scenario: Documentation, Rust-only, or other changes that cannot affect core tests
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The `changes` job performs both classifications. All 21 core test workflow calls and all three Agent Host jobs are skipped, then the always-running required-check matrix reports statuses; unchanged Compile & Hygiene may proceed independently.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Sparse checkout plus two GitHub changed-file API classifications.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One sparse checkout and two paginated list-files calls.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Only the general detector was central; core test jobs did not wait for it and were all allocated.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must complete to prove the heavy jobs can be skipped.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Start status-only Ubuntu jobs and execute jq over serialized `needs` state.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: 15 runners and 15 short shell/jq executions; six correspond to one-part Electron-Unit/Remote checks.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The workflow allocated 21 heavy core test runners plus six Browser/Smoke status reporters; there were no reporter runners for the six direct Electron-Unit/Remote statuses.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: These are the only changed core-test status operations after detection and must finish for required checks to pass.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Fixed per PR update, with API pagination scaling by changed-file count and reporter cost scaling linearly across concurrent irrelevant PRs.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No core test runners are allocated. Up to 15 lightweight required-check runners are requested after change detection/skipped dependencies resolve.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Core test caches are not restored because those jobs skip. Reporter jobs have no useful application cache; every run pays runner startup.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: skip predicates, always-running reporter matrix size, and base-vs-head job counts are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The path-based skip yields a large overall saving whose exact size depends on prior test duration. Exact reporter startup delay varies, but six avoidable VM allocations per run are certain.
Scenarios.Verdict: Overall this scenario is substantially faster because heavy tests skip. The reported finding is limited to the six unnecessary single-producer reporters and does not challenge the beneficial path-based skipping.

Scenarios.Scenario: Compile & Hygiene executes the newly added detect-changes build tests
Scenarios.CriticalPath: `Compile & Hygiene` runs `test-build-scripts` as one member of its parallel npm-run-all command and waits for it along with the other compile/hygiene tasks. The new test performs its repository scan once during that test suite.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Run `git grep -l` over tracked core test paths to find references to built-in extensions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One git subprocess per build-test suite invocation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No repository-wide extension-reference scan ran in this test suite.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The build-test task must finish before Compile & Hygiene completes, but this scan is not repeated per case or extension.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read candidate source files and check referenced extension paths.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One read per grep candidate plus bounded existence checks per textual match; grep filters the thousands of test files first.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous within the single test, after the grep result is available.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Tracked files under `src/**/test/**` and `test/unit/**`, then the much smaller set containing `extensions/<name>/` references.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One synchronous `git grep` subprocess runs in the test process, followed by sequential reads of only matching candidate files; unrelated compile checks run in parallel at the outer npm-run-all level.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No application-level cache; OS and git filesystem caches may make repeated CI/local invocations warm, but each test invocation runs one scan.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the operation and multiplicity; lower only for duration.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Candidate count and milliseconds are not measured, but the scan is a single native git operation followed by narrowed reads rather than collection-wide work inside the 18 detector cases.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: the added repository scan is bounded to once per build-test invocation and uses git grep specifically to avoid reading every test file in JavaScript, so there is insufficient evidence of a meaningful regression.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 11 changed files and all diff pages. Submitted one medium CI throughput finding for six unnecessary single-producer status runners, and recorded the PR's verified fix for serial Agent Host E2E execution. Other added work is bounded or an intentional parallelism tradeoff with a demonstrated critical-path improvement.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
